verdict.rationale: Letta exposes general interoperability surfaces — an OpenAI-compatible App Server API for clients like Open WebUI, an ACP adapter for Zed, MCP tool discovery, and 'skills' that are portable to Claude Code and Codex — which shows some cross-tool interoperability, and the community even built an unofficial MCP server bridging Letta to other agents. However, there is no first-party evidence that Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor specifically can be wired to read/write the same persistent Letta memory store as described in the story; the closest fits are generic protocol adapters and a third-party community connector rather than an official multi-assistant shared-memory integration. Missing for 10: documented first-party connectors or guides for Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor specifically consuming the same Letta memory, and evidence of bidirectional memory sync (not just tool/skill portability) across these named off-the-shelf assistants.
